findings.title: The classifier currently accepts any four-label value such as `bedrock-runtime.not-a-region.amazonaws.com` and then uses that label as the S
findings.body:
The classifier currently accepts any four-label value such as `bedrock-runtime.not-a-region.amazonaws.com` and then uses that label as the SigV4 region. AWS only accepts valid region/partition identifiers; this lets a typo or attacker-controlled `api-base` pass the recognized Bedrock path and fail later with an opaque signing/auth error (and the docs promise regional endpoints). Please validate the extracted label against the supported AWS region format (and reject empty/invalid labels) before treating it as Bedrock.

findings.title: When env/OIDC credentials win, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` and `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` are used for SigV4 but never pass through `register_secret()`
findings.body:
When env/OIDC credentials win, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` and `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` are used for SigV4 but never pass through `register_secret()`. `main()` only registers `AIPRR_API_KEY` / `AIPRR_GH_TOKEN`, so the real signing secret is absent from scrubbing. Provider HTTP errors are embedded into tracking-comment failure text via `render_tracking_body_failed` → `scrub_secrets` — any echo of the session token or secret would reach a public PR body unsanitised.

After `_resolve_aws_credentials(...)`, register each non-empty component (`access_key`, `secret_key`, `session_token`) before signing — sam

findings.title: This comment says OIDC can leave `api-key` empty, but `action.yml` marks `api-key` as `required: true` and `main()` aborts when `AIPRR_API_K
findings.body:
This comment says OIDC can leave `api-key` empty, but `action.yml` marks `api-key` as `required: true` and `main()` aborts when `AIPRR_API_KEY` is empty — so the documented "recommended" path cannot run as written.

Either relax the empty-key check for `ENDPOINT_KIND_BEDROCK` when AWS env creds are complete (and make `api-key` optional for that case), or rewrite the example/docs to require a non-empty placeholder/`api-key` even when OIDC supplies the real credentials.

findings.body:

findings.body:
**Resolved AWS credentials never go through `register_secret()`.**

`main()` only registers `AIPRR_API_KEY` and the GitHub token. On the Bedrock path the real signing material is `access_key` / `secret_key` / optional `session_token` from env (OIDC) or from unpacking the packed `api-key`. None of those component values are registered.

findings.title: Documented OIDC path says `api-key` can stay empty, but the runtime aborts without it.
findings.body:
**Documented OIDC path says `api-key` can stay empty, but the runtime aborts without it.**

`main()` still requires a non-empty `AIPRR_API_KEY` before any provider work (`if not (api_key and gh_token and …): return 1`). Credential resolution correctly prefers `AWS_*` env vars, but that code is never reached when the input is empty. A consumer who follows this comment (OIDC only, no packed secret) gets a configuration abort, not a signed Bedrock call.

Either (a) teach the example to pass a placeholder / keep a dummy `api-key` when using OIDC, or (b) relax startup so Bedrock may omit `api-key`

findings.title: These resolved AWS credentials never pass through `register_secret()`, so the outbound scrub gate (`scrub_secrets`, docs/SECURITY.md § "Secr
findings.body:
These resolved AWS credentials never pass through `register_secret()`, so the outbound scrub gate (`scrub_secrets`, docs/SECURITY.md § "Secrets") doesn't know them: the env/OIDC path registers nothing, and the packed path registers only the whole `KEY:SECRET` blob via `main()` (`scripts/reviewer.py:10358`) — a leak of just the `SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` component would post unredacted. The AWS secret is a long-lived cloud credential (bigger blast radius than the LLM key), and the agent-runner lanes have a documented echo-into-findings surface that this gate exists for.

Fix — register each component

findings.body: The canonical `host` comes from `self.profile.host` — `urlsplit().hostname`, which is lowercased and portless — while the wire `Host` header comes from `base_url`'s netloc as typed (`validate_api_base` returns `scheme://{netloc}{path}` verbatim). `api-base: https://Bedrock-Runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` or an explicit `…:443` therefore signs a host that differs byte-for-byte from the transmitted one → `InvalidSignatureException` that looks like a bad credential. Derive the signed host from `urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).netloc` (or normalise the host for this kind) so the two are structurally e

findings.title: One signature is computed here and then reused by `_post_json_with_retries` across up to 4 attempts; with `API_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 600` and de
findings.body:
One signature is computed here and then reused by `_post_json_with_retries` across up to 4 attempts; with `API_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 600` and delays `(2, 5, 15)`, the last attempt can start ~25–40 minutes after `x-amz-date` — past SigV4's ~15-minute request validity — so a throttled/5xx run would end on `InvalidSignatureException` instead of the real error. Cheap hardening: pass a header-builder callable and re-sign inside the retry loop.

findings.body:
AWS's China partition spells the runtime host `bedrock-runtime.cn-north-1.amazonaws.com.cn` — five labels, so `_is_bedrock_runtime_host` returns False and the host lands in `custom`: the run takes the non-Bedrock branch, sending the packed AWS secret as `x-api-key` (+ `anthropic-version`) to the Bedrock host, and fails with a confusing 4xx instead of SigV4. Either extend the pattern to the `.cn` suffix or fail fast with a "partition not supported" message.
